text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Low-income Portuguese families are to receive a 12,000 escudo monthly benefit for every child less than a year old, a government source told the paper.
- Retailer Sonae Distribuicao is to open eight hypermarkets in Brazil to raise its sales from 86 to 173 billion escudos by 1998. The expansion in Brazil represents a 8.5 billion escudos investment.
- Pulp company Portucel have formed a sales venture with Spain's ENCE to sell eucalyptus pulp outside Europe.
- Centre-right Social Democratic Party (PSD) leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa wants to put an end to his party's internal wrangling.
- The chairman of Casa do Douro wine company, Mesquita Montes, has accepted the government's conditions for solving the company's financial crisis.
- The cost of local telephone calls will rise by eight percent from January 1, but the price of international calls will drop more than ten percent.
- Government, unions and employers agreed to review in 1997 early retirement and to create "partial retirement".

- The ruling Socialist Party (PS) and the right-wing Popular Party (PP) deny any agreement to favour PP town councils, but one PP town councillor told the paper there had never been so much money to invest.
